title: Sum of Digits (Recursion)
directAnswer: Base case `n == 0` returns 0; else return `n % 10 + sumDigits(n / 10)`.

remember.takeaway: %10 and /10 peel digits one at a time.

problemStatement: Given a non-negative integer `n`, compute the sum of its digits recursively.
understanding: The last digit is n%10; the rest is n/10. sum(n) = n%10 + sum(n/10), base case n == 0 → 0.

approaches.name: Peel last digit
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
sum(n) = n%10 + sum(n/10), base case sum(0) = 0 — the digit-peeling idiom expressed recursively.

**Why %10 and /10.** `n % 10` is the last digit (added now); `n / 10` removes it (the smaller subproblem). Each call shortens the number by one digit until nothing is left, so the recursion depth equals the digit count.

**Why base case n == 0, not n == 1.** When n reaches 0 there are no digits left to add, so it contributes 0. Stopping at 1 would mishandle numbers ending in 0 and the input 0 itself.

**Negatives.** If negatives are allowed, take the absolute value first — the sign isn't a digit. Depth is small (≤ ~10 for ints), so stack isn't a concern here.
hints: What's the last digit, and what's 'the rest'?
Which n is the base case — 0 or 1?
approaches.complexityReasoning: one call per digit (≈ log10 n), each O(1).

java.explanation: Add the last digit, recurse on the rest.

dryRun.intro: Peel the last digit each call.

pitfalls: Negative inputs not handled (take abs first if allowed).
Base case at n == 1 instead of n == 0.

commonMistakes: Negative inputs not handled (take abs first if allowed).
Base case at n == 1 instead of n == 0.

followupVariations.title: Add Digits (digital root)
followupVariations.hint: Repeat the digit-sum to one digit.

patternNote: A core fresher pattern: Peel last digit. Master it on small inputs and it transfers to harder problems.
